changes.before: Close the introduction before the section and put Finish in its own paragraph.
changes.after: See why a browser may build a different page structure from broken HTML.

before: The source is the text you write. The DOM (Document Object Model) is the tree of elements the browser builds from that text. They can differ when the source breaks a nesting rule. A tolerant parser can recover a page without making the original source conforming HTML.

A p holds phrasing content, such as text and emphasis. A section is not phrasing content. Starting section while a paragraph is open makes the HTML parser close that paragraph first. Indentation does not override this rule.

This deliberately malformed fragment belongs in a disposable body for inspection, not in your finished page. ```html

Start

Details
Finish

``` The section becomes a sibling of the paragraph, not its child. Finish is outside the original paragraph. The unmatched closing p can also produce an empty paragraph. The DOM inspector shows the recovered tree; View Source still shows what was written.

Write separate, properly closed siblings instead. A validator checks authoring rules; a DOM inspector shows the resulting tree. Neither tool judges whether the prose is useful. For this task keep Start and Finish in their own paragraphs around the Details section. No particular browser DevTools interface is required to answer the check.
after:
The source is the HTML text you write. The DOM is the tree of elements the browser builds from it. DOM stands for Document Object Model.

A browser tries to recover from broken HTML. The page may appear, but its structure can differ from what you intended.

A `p` holds paragraph content, such as text and emphasis. A whole `section` does not belong inside it.

If a section starts while a paragraph is still open, the browser closes that paragraph first. Adding spaces to the source does not change this rule.

This example is deliberately broken. Use it to understand the mistake. ```html

Start

Details
Finish

``` The browser puts the section after the first paragraph, not inside it. Finish ends up outside that paragraph. The final `

` can also create an empty paragraph. The browser's element inspector shows the built structure. View Source shows the original text.

Fix the starter by closing the Start paragraph before the section. Put Finish in a new paragraph with `id="finish"`.

Keep `id="intro"` on the first paragraph and `id="part"` on the section. The three elements should sit beside each other, with no empty extra paragraph.

An HTML validator checks whether the source follows HTML rules. The element inspector shows how the browser read it.

before.question: A source paragraph starts, then a section starts before that paragraph is closed. Does indenting the section farther right make it a paragraph child?
choices: No. The HTML parser closes the paragraph before the section.
Yes, provided the section has an id.
before.explanation: Content rules, not indentation or id, determine how this malformed paragraph is recovered.

after.question: A source paragraph starts, then a section starts before that paragraph is closed. Does indenting the section farther right make it a paragraph child?
choices: No. The HTML parser closes the paragraph before the section.
Yes, provided the section has an id.
after.explanation: The browser follows HTML nesting rules. Extra indentation cannot put a section inside a paragraph.
